batches.test: Phase 2 nine-entry test collection (three daily sets).
batches.batch-1: First production batch: days 4-30 (with the test set, a 30-day library).

entries.text: The heart has its reasons, which reason does not know.
entries.author: Blaise Pascal
entries.original: Le cœur a ses raisons que la raison ne connaît point.
entries.notes: Pascal means intuitive knowledge of first principles, not mere sentiment.

entries.text: Yo soy yo y mi circunstancia, y si no la salvo a ella no me salvo yo.
entries.author: José Ortega y Gasset
entries.original: Yo soy yo y mi circunstancia, y si no la salvo a ella no me salvo yo.
entries.notes: Original Spanish; 1914 text, public domain in the US.

entries.text: Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly, then woke unsure which of them was doing the dreaming.
entries.author: Zhuangzi
entries.work: Zhuangzi, ch. 2 "Qiwulun" (Discussion on Making All Things Equal)
entries.original: 昔者莊周夢為胡蝶……不知周之夢為胡蝶與，胡蝶之夢為周與？
entries.translation: Original summary; compare James Legge (1891, public domain)
entries.notes: Summary, not a quotation. Zhuangzi asks whether Zhou dreamed the butterfly or the butterfly dreams Zhou.

entries.text: Can you choose what you find convincing?
entries.notes: Doxastic voluntarism. Deliberately short to test the minimum length.

entries.text: If you could erase your worst memory, would the person left still be you?
entries.notes: Locke's memory theory of personal identity.

entries.text: A ship has every plank replaced, one at a time. At which plank did it become a different ship?
entries.notes: Ship of Theseus (Plutarch). Deliberately long to test three-line fit.

entries.subject: space
entries.text: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
entries.notes: One rotation ~243 Earth days (sidereal); one orbit ~225 Earth days. Sunrise-to-sunrise is ~117 days, so 'day' means one full spin.

entries.subject: neuroscience
entries.text: Each eye has a blind spot with no light sensors. Your brain quietly paints over the gap.
entries.notes: Optic disc lacks photoreceptors; perceptual filling-in. With both eyes open, the other eye also covers the gap.

entries.subject: history
entries.text: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
entries.notes: Great Pyramid completed c. 2560 BCE; Cleopatra died 30 BCE (~2,530 years later); Apollo 11 landed 1969 (~2,000 years after her death).

entries.text: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent.
entries.author: Laozi

entries.text: One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
entries.author: Albert Camus

entries.text: Lo bueno, si breve, dos veces bueno.
entries.author: Baltasar Gracián
entries.work: Oráculo manual y arte de prudencia (1647), aforismo 105
entries.original: Lo bueno, si breve, dos veces bueno.
entries.notes: Original Spanish, public domain.

entries.text: Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions.
entries.author: David Hume

entries.text: Ibn Sina imagined a man floating in empty air, senses cut off. Would he still know he exists?
entries.author: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
entries.work: Kitāb al-Shifāʾ, De Anima — the 'Floating Man'
entries.notes: Ibn Sina's answer: yes, the soul would affirm its own existence.

entries.text: He who fights with monsters should be careful lest he thereby become a monster.
entries.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
entries.original: Wer mit Ungeheuern kämpft, mag zusehn, dass er nicht dabei zum Ungeheuer wird.

entries.text: Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
entries.author: Simone Weil
entries.original: L'attention est la forme la plus rare et la plus pure de la générosité.

entries.text: Heraclitus held that you cannot step into the same river twice: the waters are always new.
entries.author: Heraclitus
entries.work: Fragment B12; reported in Plato, Cratylus 402a

entries.text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
entries.author: Epictetus

entries.text: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
entries.author: Simone de Beauvoir
entries.original: On ne naît pas femme : on le devient.

entries.text: Si Aristóteles hubiera guisado, mucho más hubiera escrito.
entries.display_attribution: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
entries.author: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
entries.work: Respuesta a sor Filotea de la Cruz (1691)
entries.notes: Mexican philosopher-poet; defending women's right to study.

entries.text: Spinoza argued we feel free because we know our desires, but not the causes behind them.
entries.author: Baruch Spinoza
entries.work: Ethics (1677), Part I Appendix; Part II, Prop. 35 Scholium

entries.text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought.
entries.author: The Dhammapada (Buddhist scripture)

entries.text: Arendt argued that terrible evil can be done by ordinary people who simply stop thinking.
entries.author: Hannah Arendt
entries.work: Eichmann in Jerusalem (1963) — 'the banality of evil'

entries.text: Asked where he came from, Diogenes said: “I am a citizen of the world.”
entries.author: Diogenes of Sinope
entries.work: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers VI.63
entries.translation: R. D. Hicks (1925, public domain); framing lightly adapted

entries.text: Kierkegaard noted that life is understood backwards, but must be lived forwards.
entries.author: Søren Kierkegaard

entries.text: Nāgārjuna taught that nothing exists by itself; everything arises from something else.
entries.author: Nāgārjuna
entries.translation: Original summary of dependent origination and emptiness

entries.text: The life which is unexamined is not worth living.
entries.author: Socrates (via Plato)

entries.text: Toda la vida es sueño, y los sueños, sueños son.
entries.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
entries.work: La vida es sueño (1635), Jornada II
entries.original: que toda la vida es sueño, / y los sueños, sueños son.
entries.notes: Closing lines of Segismundo's monologue; leading 'que' dropped.

entries.text: Confucius said real knowledge is knowing what you know and admitting what you don't.
entries.author: Confucius
entries.original: 知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。

entries.text: Schopenhauer saw human life swinging like a pendulum between pain and boredom.
entries.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
entries.work: The World as Will and Representation (1818), §57

entries.text: All men by nature desire to know.
entries.author: Aristotle

entries.text: Ibn Rushd argued that truth cannot contradict truth, so reason and faith must agree.
entries.author: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)

entries.text: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
entries.author: Marcus Aurelius

entries.text: Montaigne held that every person carries the whole form of the human condition.
entries.author: Michel de Montaigne

entries.text: Epicurus argued we need not fear death: when it comes, we are no longer there to suffer it.
entries.author: Epicurus

entries.text: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
entries.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
entries.original: Wovon man nicht sprechen kann, darüber muss man schweigen.

entries.text: Is it possible to want something you've never imagined?
If no one would ever find out, would it still matter that you lied?
Would you take a pill that made you content with your life exactly as it is?
If you met yourself from ten years ago, who would be more disappointed?
¿Eres la misma persona que fuiste de niño, o solo llevas su nombre?
If an AI said it was suffering, what would convince you it wasn't?
Which of your opinions would change if you had been born a century earlier?
If time travel is possible, why hasn't anyone from the future visited?
Is it braver to change your mind or to keep a promise you no longer believe in?
Can you be wrong about whether you are in pain?
Is a perfect forgery worth less than the original? If so, what are you paying for?
Do you own your attention, or does whatever is loudest own it?
If everyone forgave everything, would justice still mean anything?
Si nadie te recordara, ¿tu vida habría importado menos?
Would living forever make your choices more meaningful, or less?
If animals could tell us what they think of us, would you want to hear it?
When you lose an argument, how often do you lose the belief too?
Is it fair to judge people of the past by the morals of the present?
What would you still do if no one could ever see the results?
Can a society be free if no one in it disagrees?
Is boredom a problem to solve, or a signal worth listening to?
Does a tree falling in an empty forest make a sound, or only a vibration?
¿Qué creencia tuya defenderías aunque nadie más la compartiera?
If every choice could be undone, would any choice really matter?
Which do you trust more: what you remember, or what you wrote down at the time?
If you could know exactly how every stranger saw you, would you want to?
If you could ask the universe one yes-or-no question, what would you ask?

entries.subject: biology
entries.text: An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue because it uses copper instead of iron.
entries.notes: Hemocyanin (copper-based) carries oxygen; two branchial hearts plus one systemic heart.

entries.subject: history
entries.text: Teaching at Oxford began by 1096, more than 200 years before the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlán.
entries.notes: Tenochtitlán founded c. 1325; Aztec Triple Alliance 1428.

entries.subject: psychology
entries.text: About half of people in a 1998 study didn't notice their conversation partner being swapped.
entries.notes: Simons & Levin (1998), 'door study': 7 of 15 pedestrians failed to notice.

entries.subject: space
entries.text: A sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
entries.notes: NASA Imagine the Universe: ~1 trillion kg per sugar cube.

entries.subject: biology
entries.text: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings, shaped by uneven stiffness in their intestines.
entries.notes: Yang et al., Soft Matter (2021).

entries.subject: mathematics
entries.text: Around 300 BCE, Euclid proved there are infinitely many prime numbers. The proof still holds.
entries.notes: Elements, Book IX, Prop. 20.

entries.subject: history
entries.text: Tree rings show Vikings were cutting wood in Newfoundland in 1021, centuries before Columbus.
entries.notes: Kuitems et al., Nature (2021); dated via the 993 CE solar storm signal.

entries.subject: physics
entries.text: Lightning heats the air to about 50,000°F, roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
entries.notes: NOAA / National Weather Service.

entries.subject: psychology
entries.text: Hand people a face they didn't choose, and most will explain why they chose it.
entries.notes: Choice blindness: Johansson, Hall et al., Science 310 (2005). Only ~13% detected the swap.

entries.subject: nature
entries.text: Pando, a single aspen in Utah, has about 47,000 trunks sharing one root system.
entries.notes: Fishlake National Forest; ~6,000 tonnes, ~106 acres.

entries.subject: chemistry / space
entries.text: Helium was found on the Sun in 1868, nearly three decades before it was found on Earth.
entries.notes: Solar spectrum line 1868 (Janssen, Lockyer); isolated on Earth by Ramsay, 1895.

entries.subject: history
entries.text: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, often called the shortest in history, lasted under an hour.
entries.notes: Usually given as 38–45 minutes (27 August 1896).

entries.subject: evolution
entries.text: Sharks were swimming in the oceans tens of millions of years before the first trees grew.
entries.notes: Sharks ~450 Mya (earliest evidence); trees ~385–390 Mya. Exact gap depends on what counts as a shark.

entries.subject: neuroscience
entries.text: El cerebro pesa cerca del 2% del cuerpo, pero consume alrededor del 20% de su energía.
entries.notes: Raichle & Gusnard, PNAS (2002), 'Appraising the brain's energy budget'.

entries.subject: space / engineering
entries.text: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is farther from Earth than any other object humans have made.
entries.notes: Entered interstellar space in 2012.

entries.subject: psychology
entries.text: Researchers got about 1 in 4 people to “remember” a childhood event that never happened.
entries.notes: Loftus & Pickrell (1995), 'lost in the mall': 25% of 24 participants.

entries.subject: geology
entries.text: The rock at the top of Mount Everest is limestone that formed on an ancient seafloor.
entries.notes: Qomolangma Formation, Ordovician; contains trilobite and crinoid fragments.

entries.subject: mathematics
entries.text: 0.999… repeating forever is exactly equal to 1, not just very close to it.
entries.notes: Standard real-analysis result (e.g., 1/3 = 0.333…, times 3).

entries.subject: engineering
entries.text: Roman harbor concrete gets stronger in seawater, as new minerals crystallize inside it.
entries.notes: Jackson et al., American Mineralogist (2017): Al-tobermorite and phillipsite growth.

entries.subject: nature / space
entries.text: Tardigrades survived ten days exposed to the vacuum of space, then reproduced back on Earth.
entries.notes: Jönsson et al., Current Biology (2008), FOTON-M3.

entries.subject: geology / space
entries.text: About 70 million years ago, a day on Earth lasted roughly 23.5 hours.
entries.notes: de Winter et al. (2020), rudist clam growth rings: 372 days per year.

entries.subject: psychology / medicine
entries.text: Placebos can still ease some symptoms even when patients are told they're taking a placebo.
entries.notes: Open-label placebo trials, mainly IBS and other subjective symptoms (Kaptchuk 2010; Lembo 2021).

entries.subject: biology
entries.text: Botanically, bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
entries.notes: Strawberry is an accessory (aggregate) fruit.

entries.subject: animal behavior
entries.text: Crows remember the faces of people who threatened them, and teach other crows to scold them.
entries.notes: Marzluff et al., University of Washington; Proc. R. Soc. B.

entries.subject: chemistry
entries.text: At one exact temperature and pressure, water can exist as ice, liquid, and vapor at once.
entries.notes: Triple point: 0.01 °C at 611.657 Pa.

entries.subject: ecology
entries.text: Scientists estimate about half of Earth's oxygen is produced in the ocean, mostly by plankton.
entries.notes: NOAA estimate.

entries.subject: mathematics
entries.text: There are estimated to be more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
entries.notes: Shannon number ~10^120 games vs ~10^80 atoms (estimates).
